rules.title: Tenant screening fee limits and required refunds/disclosures
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a prospective tenant a screening fee only for permissible screening costs and may not charge it if no rental unit is actually available. The applicant should receive a credit-report copy within 7 days after the landlord receives it, a receipt and itemized accounting, and a refund of any unused portion; if the applicant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when a landlord charges a prospective tenant a screening fee to obtain information such as a consumer credit report; other statutory coverage details are not stated in the document.
coverage.summary: Prospective tenants applying for available rental units are covered when a landlord charges a tenant screening fee.

rules.exemptions: The landlord must return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, unless the landlord has a policy to review applications in the order received, rent to the first qualified applicant, and not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.
rules.interaction: The Berkeley page states that screening and application fee limits exist under both state and local law, and Berkeley requires owners to disclose the state fee cap and rights statement before taking a fee.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96
Landlords may use screening fees to obtain information about a prospective tenant like a consumer credit report. Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening and application fee disclosures and limits
rules.requirement: When a Berkeley residential rental owner or agent charges a fee to buy a consumer credit report or process an application, the owner must give a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and state the maximum fee cap before receiving the fee. An owner or agent also may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add, replace, or remove a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.key_value: Disclosure of California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b) maximum fee cap; no non-refundable application-related fees for existing tenancies

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when an owner or agent receives a request to rent residential property in Berkeley and charges a consumer-credit-report or application-processing fee; also applies to existing tenants renewing or changing roommates.
coverage.summary: Berkeley residential rental applications involving screening/application fees, and existing Berkeley residential tenancies involving renewal or roommate-change fees, are covered.

rules.penalty: Chapter 13.78 applies regardless of contrary lease language, and any provision of an existing rental agreement or lease that violates the chapter is unenforceable.
rules.interaction: The Berkeley ordinance requires disclosure of rights and the maximum cap under California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b) and applies despite contrary language in rental agreements.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
